newsitem.title: USA: Uncle B's, Heinz cancel contract.
newsitem.headline: Uncle B's, Heinz cancel contract.

text.p: Uncle B's Bakery Inc and Heinz Bakery Products have agreed to cancel their existing contract to produce frozen raw dough bagels and to form another partnership, Uncle B's said on Wednesday.
Uncle B's said the cancelation would have an adverse impact on sales and net income for its fiscal third and fourth quarters, with the major sales impact occurring in the fourth quarter.
The move was taken because of problems encountered with ingredients provided by outside suppliers, which hindered Uncle B's ability to deliver the product, the company said.
Uncle B's in a statement said it believed it should not absorb the additional costs of customer specification changes not contained in its original agreement.
The company could not be reached immediately for further comment.

Under the new strategic partnership agreement, Heinz Bakery Products, part of H.J. Heinz Co, designated Uncle B's as its preferred supplier of par baked and fully baked bagels. The new agreement covers a term of three years with no guaranteed volumes, Uncle B's said.

As a result of the change, Uncle B's said it now expected sales of $20 million to $21 million for its fiscal year ending July 31. Previously, the company estimated fiscal 1997 sales at $24 million to $26 million.
The company reported fiscal 1996 sales of $17.4 million and fiscal 1997 first-half sales of $11.8 million.
Uncle B's produces and markets the Uncle B's and Millspring brands of bagels. The company's products are currently available in 11,000 supermarkets in 43 states.
Shares of Uncle B's were off 3/8 to 1-1/4 late Wednesday afternoon.
